name: Healthcare Services and Physician Practice Roll-Ups
summary: Physician practice management platforms and MSO/friendly-PC structures, nursing homes and senior care, behavioral health, home health and hospital sale-leasebacks. Revenue is set by payors, so diligence centers on reimbursement durability (payor mix, contracts, fee schedules, out-of-network exposure), revenue traced from 835 remittances to bank deposits, independent per-provider coding audits, fraud-and-abuse compliance (Anti-Kickback Statute, Stark, False Claims Act reaching sponsors), FMV support for every referral-source arrangement, corporate practice of medicine and state PE-healthcare notice laws (Oregon SB 951 as the strictest template), antitrust risk of serial sub-HSR add-ons, sale-leaseback rent coverage, and for nursing homes the staffing and quality evidence (PE ownership raised short-term mortality about 10% to 11%). Behavioral health and home health are named as roll-up platforms but not treated separately in the bible; numeric revenue-cycle and productivity thresholds were not sourced (GAP).
one_check: Rebuild revenue from remittances and bank deposits and run an independent coding audit per provider before close; payor-set revenue that cannot be traced to cash, or that depends on outlier coding or above-FMV referral arrangements, is the liability, not the asset.

subtypes.name: Physician practice roll-up
subtypes.description: Platform practice plus add-ons (dermatology, anesthesia, GI, dental and similar) with centralized billing.

subtypes.name: MSO / friendly-PC structure
subtypes.description: Sponsor-owned MSO contracting with a physician-owned professional entity where CPOM applies.

subtypes.name: Nursing homes / senior care / post-acute
subtypes.description: Skilled nursing and post-acute facilities; government payors about 75% of revenue; staffing and quality evidence.

subtypes.name: Behavioral health
subtypes.description: Behavioral-health practice or facility roll-up (named platform type; general items applied).

subtypes.name: Home health
subtypes.description: Home-health agency roll-up (named platform type; general items applied).

intake_questions.question: Is the target a physician practice roll-up, an MSO/friendly-PC structure, nursing homes or senior care, behavioral health, or home health?
In which states does the business operate, and do any have CPOM or PE-healthcare notice laws?
intake_questions.why: Drives state CPOM and notice workstreams.

intake_questions.question: What share of revenue is Medicare, Medicaid, commercial and out-of-network?
intake_questions.why: Reimbursement durability and No Surprises Act exposure.

intake_questions.question: Has the business done a sale-leaseback or does it plan one?
How many add-ons has the platform done, and have they been integrated onto one billing system?
When was the last external coding audit?
intake_questions.why: No audit in three years is a red flag.

requests.request: Payor mix by revenue and by visit for 36 months (Medicare, Medicaid, commercial by payor, self-pay, out-of-network).
requests.why: Payors set price; government payors are about 75% of nursing-home revenue.
requests.pass: Mix reported monthly and ties to 835 remittances; no single payor dominance unaddressed.
requests.fail: Mix only from gross charges or not tied to remittances.

requests.request: Top payor contracts with rates, escalators and renewal dates.
requests.why: Payor rate cuts and renewals drive EBITDA.
requests.pass: Renewal dates known; no top-payor renewal inside 12 months without a plan.
requests.fail: Top payor renewal imminent with rate risk.
requests.verify: Confirm in-network status with the payor portal.

requests.request: CPT-level volume and reimbursement trend for 36 months.
requests.why: Coding shifts and fee-schedule changes.
requests.pass: Trends explained by volume, not coding mix shift.

requests.request: Monthly revenue-cycle KPIs for 36 months: days in A/R, initial denial rate, net collection rate, A/R over 90 days.
requests.why: Revenue-cycle quality; specific numeric thresholds were not sourced (GAP).
requests.pass: KPIs stable or improving and benchmarked against HFMA MAP Keys peer data.
requests.fail: Deteriorating trends or no KPIs tracked.

requests.request: Licenses, DEA registrations and accreditations for every site and provider.
requests.format: Copies with expiry dates; state board lookups.
requests.why: Operating without licenses voids reimbursement.
requests.pass: All current; none under restriction.

requests.request: Legal structure chart: MSO, professional entities (friendly-physician PCs), ownership and the management agreements between them.
requests.format: Chart with ownership percentages and contracts.
requests.why: CPOM bars non-physician ownership in many states.
requests.pass: Structure CPOM-compliant in each state.
requests.fail: Sponsor directly owns practices in CPOM states.

requests.request: State footprint with state CPOM analysis and state PE-healthcare transaction-notice or approval requirements.
requests.why: Oregon SB 951 is the strictest CPOM template; several states enacted notice or oversight laws in 2024-25.
requests.pass: Every state analyzed; notice requirements and timelines listed.

requests.request: Add-on acquisition history: each add-on, price multiple, date, and the platform multiple.
requests.why: The platform-versus-add-on multiple spread is the thesis.
requests.pass: Add-on multiples and integration status disclosed.
requests.fail: Thesis rests on arbitrage with no integration.

requests.request: Real estate: leases, sale-leaseback agreements, landlord identity and relationships.
requests.why: Sale-leasebacks funding dividends weakened Steward.
requests.pass: Landlords unaffiliated or disclosed; rents at market.

requests.request: Nursing-home and post-acute quality file: staffing ratios, CMS Five-Star history, survey deficiencies.
requests.format: CMS Care Compare data and state survey reports for 5 years.
requests.why: PE ownership raised short-term mortality about 10% to 11% and cut nursing-assistant hours about 3%.
requests.pass: Staffing ratios and Five-Star stable or improving after prior acquisitions; no immediate-jeopardy citations.
requests.fail: Falling staffing or star ratings after acquisition.

requests.request: MSO management services agreement and fee formula.
requests.why: Percentage-of-collections MSO fees are a known AKS risk area.
requests.pass: Flat or cost-plus fee supported by FMV.
requests.fail: Fee as a percentage of collections without counsel support.

requests.request: Friendly-physician ownership agreements, stock transfer restriction and succession agreements.
requests.why: CPOM structure unwinds if the friendly physician leaves.
requests.pass: Succession agreement allows prompt substitution compliant with state law.
requests.verify: Counsel review against state CPOM law.

requests.request: Escrow or special indemnity for pre-close billing liabilities and R&W insurance exclusions.
requests.why: Upcoding and kickback liabilities survive closing.
requests.pass: Escrow or special indemnity sized to coding-audit findings.
requests.fail: Known billing issues excluded from R&W with no special indemnity.

requests.request: Provider employment agreements: compensation formulas, noncompetes and term.
requests.why: Compensation tied to referrals implicates Stark; noncompetes void in some states.
requests.pass: Compensation FMV-supported and not referral-based; noncompetes enforceable where relied on.
requests.fail: Referral-linked pay or void noncompetes relied on.

requests.request: Physician rollover equity and vesting terms tied to tenure.
requests.why: Physicians leave after earn-outs.
requests.pass: Rollover with vesting tied to tenure.

requests.request: Fund ownership structure analysis for ERISA multiemployer withdrawal liability (80% common control) and control-person exposure.
requests.why: Sun Capital funds held to be a trade or business under common control.
requests.pass: Ownership structured below 80% common control where withdrawal liability exists; formalities observed.

requests.request: D&O coverage at fund and company level.
requests.why: FCA liability can reach the sponsor.
requests.pass: Coverage at both levels with regulatory exclusions understood.

requests.request: Timeline for state transaction notices or approvals and any antitrust filings.
requests.why: State notice laws and FTC scrutiny of serial add-ons.
requests.pass: All filings scheduled before closing.

requests.request: Remittance files (835) and bank deposits for 36 months, for a revenue rebuild.
requests.format: Raw 835 files from the clearinghouse and bank statements from the bank.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: payor-set revenue that cannot be traced to cash is the liability.
requests.pass: Net revenue rebuilt from remittances ties to reported net revenue and to deposits within 2%.
requests.fail: Gaps between remittances, deposits and reported revenue.

requests.request: Contractual-allowance estimates tested against cash collected.
requests.why: Overstated net revenue via allowance assumptions.
requests.pass: Allowances true up to cash within 2%.

requests.request: Payor concentration: largest commercial payor as % of revenue and renewal date.
requests.why: Payor rate cuts.
requests.pass: Concentration and renewal risk modelled.

requests.request: Impact analysis of the latest annual CMS Medicare physician fee schedule rule on revenue.
requests.why: Medicare fee-schedule changes.
requests.pass: Impact quantified in the model.

requests.request: In-network status by payor and share of revenue from out-of-network billing, with No Surprises Act arbitration exposure.
requests.why: Out-of-network economics changed with the No Surprises Act process from 2022 (not primary-sourced).
requests.pass: Out-of-network revenue small and declining.

requests.request: Billing and coding audit results for the last 3 years.
requests.why: No billing audit in three years is a red flag.
requests.pass: External audit within 3 years with remediated findings.
requests.verify: Independent coding audit in third-party stage.

requests.request: Compliance program documents and hotline log.
requests.format: Program, policies, hotline log for 3 years.
requests.why: DOJ asks whether the acquirer did pre-acquisition compliance diligence.
requests.pass: Program with compliance officer, training and investigated hotline reports.

requests.request: Prior self-disclosures and overpayment refunds, with dates identified and refunded.
requests.why: Overpayments must be refunded within 60 days.
requests.pass: All identified overpayments refunded within 60 days.

requests.request: OIG exclusion (LEIE) and SAM screening results for every provider and employee.
requests.why: Providers with prior exclusions.
requests.pass: No excluded individuals; monthly screening.
requests.verify: Run our own LEIE and SAM checks.

requests.request: Production by provider and the number of providers producing the top 50% of revenue.
requests.why: Physicians leaving after earn-outs.
requests.pass: Revenue not concentrated in a few providers without retention.
requests.fail: Few providers produce most revenue with no retention.

requests.request: Post-close provider compensation compared with pre-close compensation.
requests.why: Pay cuts drive departures.
requests.pass: Changes modelled with retention plan.

requests.request: Noncompete enforceability by state, including Oregon SB 951 voiding of noncompetition, nondisclosure and nondisparagement agreements.
requests.why: Noncompetes are void in some states.
requests.pass: Model does not rely on unenforceable noncompetes.

requests.request: Add-on purchase agreements with fair-market-value opinions.
requests.why: Paying above FMV for a referral source implicates AKS and Stark.
requests.pass: Every add-on price supported by an independent FMV opinion.

requests.request: Medical directorships and all other referral-source arrangements with FMV and commercial-reasonableness support.
requests.why: Above-FMV directorships are kickback-tainted.
requests.pass: Every arrangement in writing, FMV-supported, commercially reasonable, with time records.

requests.request: AKS and Stark analysis of the MSO fee structure.
requests.why: Percentage-of-revenue fees are a known risk area.
requests.pass: Structure fits a safe harbor or counsel concludes low risk.

requests.request: Malpractice claims history and tail coverage.
requests.why: Unfunded claims.
requests.pass: Tail coverage in place for departing providers and pre-close acts.

requests.request: Integration test for each add-on: billing system and payor contracts consolidated.
requests.why: Add-ons never integrated; add-ons on separate billing systems years after acquisition.
requests.pass: All add-ons older than 12 months on one billing system and platform payor contracts.

requests.request: Local market share by specialty and price changes after each add-on.
requests.why: Price-driven EBITDA in concentrated markets drew the FTC suit against USAP and Welsh Carson.
requests.pass: No dominant local share; EBITDA growth not price-driven.
requests.fail: Price increases after add-ons in concentrated markets.

requests.request: History of serial add-ons below HSR thresholds and any FTC or state inquiries.
requests.why: HSR thresholds are not a safe harbor.
requests.pass: Antitrust risk assessed.

requests.request: Rent coverage after any sale-leaseback, with escalators, and a trace of where the proceeds went.
requests.why: Steward's $1.25B sale-leaseback funded dividends and left escalating rents.
requests.pass: Rent coverage adequate through escalators; proceeds reinvested, not dividended.
requests.fail: Proceeds paid as dividends; coverage falls with escalators.

requests.request: Related-party landlord review: friendly physician or sponsor affiliate as landlord.
requests.why: Friendly physician owning the MSO's landlord is a red flag.
requests.pass: No related-party landlords, or at FMV with disclosure.

requests.request: Nursing-assistant hours per patient-day and staffing ratios by facility, before and after prior acquisitions.
requests.why: PE ownership cut frontline staffing about 3%.
requests.pass: Staffing stable or rising.

requests.request: Fees, leases and interest paid to related parties or landlords by each facility.
requests.why: Costs shifted to monitoring fees, interest and lease payments.
requests.pass: Related-party payments at FMV and small.

requests.request: Government payor share and exposure to Medicaid and Medicare rate changes.
requests.why: Government payors about 75% of nursing-home revenue.
requests.pass: Rate sensitivity modelled.

requests.request: Compliance-diligence scope and gaps memo for the IC.
requests.why: DOJ Evaluation of Corporate Compliance Programs.
requests.pass: Scope and gaps documented.

requests.request: 100-day compliance integration plan.
requests.why: DOJ expects prompt integration and post-close audits.
requests.pass: Plan in the value-creation plan.

requests.request: Statement of sponsor involvement in billing, marketing and referral practices of portfolio companies.
requests.why: DOJ named Riordan Lewis & Haden for financing a kickback scheme ($21.36M, 2019).
requests.pass: No sponsor direction of marketing or referral practices.

requests.request: Peer-benchmark outlier billing analysis by provider.
requests.format: Analysis against public Medicare utilization data.
requests.why: Upcoding or medically unnecessary services inflating EBITDA.
requests.pass: No outlier providers, or outliers explained.

requests.request: Provider productivity in wRVUs per FTE against MGMA benchmarks.
requests.why: Provider productivity (thresholds not sourced; GAP).
requests.pass: Productivity benchmarked.

requests.request: Healthcare regulatory counsel memo on AKS, Stark, CPOM and state notice laws.
requests.why: Fraud-and-abuse and ownership-law exposure.
requests.pass: No unmitigated high-risk findings.

requests.request: Independent coding audit on a statistically valid sample per provider.
requests.why: THE ONE CHECK: outlier coding is the liability.
requests.pass: Error rate low with no systematic upcoding; findings feed escrow.

requests.request: FMV and commercial-reasonableness appraisal of physician compensation and add-on prices.
requests.why: Above-FMV referral payments.
requests.pass: All within FMV.

requests.request: Revenue-cycle QoE with remittance-to-cash rebuild.
requests.why: Revenue not traceable to cash.
requests.pass: Rebuild ties within 2%.

requests.request: Antitrust counsel analysis of serial add-ons.
requests.why: FTC v. USAP and Welsh Carson.
requests.pass: Low risk.

requests.request: Real estate appraisal and lease review for sale-leasebacks.
requests.why: Escalating rents.
requests.pass: Market rents and coverage adequate.

requests.request: Malpractice and tail-coverage broker review.
requests.why: Uninsured claims.
requests.pass: Adequate limits and tail.

requests.request: Executed escrow or special indemnity for pre-close billing.
requests.why: Pre-close billing liability.
requests.pass: Executed and sized to audit findings.

requests.request: Evidence that all state notices were filed and waiting periods expired or approvals obtained.
requests.why: State PE-healthcare laws.
requests.pass: All complete.

requests.request: Bound tail coverage for pre-close acts.
requests.why: Uninsured claims.
requests.pass: Bound.

requests.request: Executed friendly-physician succession and stock-transfer agreements.
requests.why: CPOM unwind.
requests.pass: Executed.

requests.request: Executed provider agreements and rollover equity documents.
requests.why: Provider departures.
requests.pass: Executed.

requests.request: Monthly revenue-cycle KPI report.
requests.why: Revenue-cycle deterioration.
requests.pass: Stable against HFMA peer data.

requests.request: Quarterly payor-mix and contract-renewal report.
requests.why: Rate cuts.
requests.pass: No surprises.

requests.request: Annual external coding audit.
requests.why: No billing audit in three years.
requests.pass: Annual audit with remediation.

requests.request: Monthly OIG/SAM rescreening confirmation.
requests.why: Excluded providers.
requests.pass: No exclusions.

requests.request: Quarterly compliance report: hotline, overpayment refunds, self-disclosures.
requests.why: Unrefunded overpayments.
requests.pass: Refunds within 60 days.

requests.request: Quarterly staffing ratios and Five-Star ratings by facility.
requests.why: Quality decline.
requests.pass: Stable or improving.

requests.request: Post-close compliance audit of each acquired entity within 12 months.
requests.why: DOJ expects post-close audits.
requests.pass: Completed with remediation.

requests.request: Annual rent-coverage report.
requests.why: Escalating rents.
requests.pass: Adequate coverage.

requests.request: Annual update of state CPOM and PE-healthcare law changes affecting the footprint.
requests.why: Oregon-style laws spreading.
requests.pass: Structure remains compliant.

kill_tests.test: Net revenue cannot be traced from 835 remittances to bank deposits within 2%.
Independent coding audit shows systematic upcoding not covered by escrow or special indemnity.
Any provider currently excluded by OIG or SAM.
Referral-source arrangements or add-on prices without FMV support that counsel cannot cure before close.
Ownership structure violates a state's CPOM law (e.g. Oregon SB 951 control prohibitions).
Sale-leaseback proceeds paid as dividends with rent coverage failing under escalators.

red_flags.flag: EBITDA growth driven by price in concentrated local markets.
MSO fee as a % of collections.
No billing audit in three years.
Friendly physician who also owns the MSO's landlord.
Sale-leaseback proceeds used for dividends; escalating rents.
Staffing ratios falling after acquisition; Five-Star rating declining.
Fees, interest and rent paid to sponsor affiliates or related landlords.
Add-ons on separate billing systems years after acquisition.
Serial add-ons below HSR thresholds in one local market.
Overpayments identified but not refunded within 60 days.
Sponsor involvement in marketing or referral practices.

metrics.source: Gupta, Howell, Yannelis and Gupta, NBER w28474

metrics.acceptable: Nursing-assistant hours per patient-day about -3%; ours must not fall post-acquisition
1,674 acquisitions in 128 deals among about 12,400 for-profit homes
About 6% (6.4% WP); up to about 50 a year; cluster just below HSR thresholds

metrics.metric: Riordan, Lewis & Haden / Diabetic Care Rx FCA settlement
metrics.acceptable: $21.36M, 2019 per HLS Forum (general lane said 2021; confirm on justice.gov)
Days in A/R and denial rates against HFMA MAP Keys peer data; numeric thresholds not sourced (GAP)
wRVUs per FTE against MGMA benchmarks; thresholds not sourced (GAP)
Remittance-based net revenue within 2% of reported and of deposits
Keep fund ownership below 80% common control where withdrawal liability exists
metrics.source: Sun Capital (D. Mass. 2018) via HLS Forum 2019

third_party_reports.report: Regulatory memo (AKS, Stark, CPOM, state notice laws)

third_party_reports.provider: Independent coding auditor (statistically valid sample per provider)

third_party_reports.required_when: Any physician compensation, referral-source arrangement or add-on purchase

third_party_reports.report: Real estate appraisal and lease review
third_party_reports.provider: Real estate appraiser and lease reviewer

hard_questions.question: What share of revenue comes from the top payor, and when does that contract renew?
hard_questions.good_answer: A precise share and date with a renewal plan and rate sensitivity.

hard_questions.question: What did the last external coding audit find?
hard_questions.good_answer: A recent audit with low error rates and documented remediation.

hard_questions.question: Show FMV support for every arrangement with a referral source.
hard_questions.good_answer: Written agreements with independent FMV and commercial-reasonableness opinions and time logs.

hard_questions.question: Which add-ons are still on separate billing systems?
Which state laws require notice or approval for this deal, and does any state's CPOM law reach the MSO structure?
hard_questions.good_answer: A state-by-state counsel memo with filings scheduled.

hard_questions.question: Who is the friendly physician, and what happens if he or she leaves?
hard_questions.good_answer: A named physician with an executed succession agreement allowing prompt substitution.

hard_questions.question: After the sale-leaseback, what is rent coverage, and where did the proceeds go?
hard_questions.good_answer: Adequate coverage through escalators and proceeds reinvested, not dividended.

hard_questions.question: What happened to staffing ratios and quality ratings at prior acquisitions?
hard_questions.good_answer: Stable or improving, from CMS data.

failure_cases.what_happened: Sale-leaseback of hospital real estate to MPT ($1.25B for Massachusetts) funded dividends and left escalating rents.
failure_cases.check: Model rent coverage after any sale-leaseback; trace where the proceeds went.

failure_cases.case: Riordan, Lewis & Haden / Diabetic Care Rx
failure_cases.what_happened: DOJ named the PE sponsor alongside its portfolio pharmacy for financing a kickback scheme; $21.36M.
failure_cases.check: Pre-close billing and referral diligence; sponsor involvement in marketing practices.

failure_cases.year: FTC suit 2023 (dates and order terms weak; verify on ftc.gov)
failure_cases.what_happened: Serial roll-up of Texas anesthesia practices followed by price increases; Welsh Carson later entered an FTC consent order requiring prior notice of certain acquisitions.
failure_cases.check: Local market share by specialty; price increases after add-ons; state notice requirements.

failure_cases.what_happened: Mortality up about 10% to 11%; staffing down about 3%; costs shifted to fees, interest, leases.
failure_cases.check: Staffing ratios; Five-Star trend; related-party fees and leases; rent coverage.

failure_cases.what_happened: PE funds held to be a trade or business under common control with a bankrupt portfolio company because of active management and control.
failure_cases.check: Structure fund ownership below 80% common control; observe formalities.
Independent coding audit and peer-benchmark outlier analysis before close; escrow or special indemnity.

failure_cases.what_happened: Above-FMV medical directorships, MSO percentage fees.
failure_cases.check: FMV opinions; healthcare regulatory counsel review.

failure_cases.case: Payor rate cuts or out-of-network revenue collapse (generic)
failure_cases.check: In-network status by payor; out-of-network share of revenue.
Rollover equity and vesting tied to tenure; production concentration.

failure_cases.case: Antitrust or state-law block of add-ons (generic)
failure_cases.check: Local share by specialty; state notice requirements.
One billing system and one payor contract test.

failure_cases.what_happened: Friendly physician leaves or an Oregon-style law voids control.
failure_cases.check: Friendly-physician succession agreements; state-by-state CPOM analysis.
